evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: Behavior: first-year students in 12 public secondary schools in Cusco attend the free after-school math sessions twice a week. Attendance falls from 70% to 30% after the first graded quiz in week 4. Sessions are free, at their own school, and end before the last bus. We interviewed 24 students who stopped coming: 15 said some version of 'I got a bad mark, so math is not for me', 9 said 'the ones who stay are the ones who were always good', 4 said they have to help at home those afternoons. Students can retake each quiz once and tutors review every wrong answer the next session. The ministry wants a growth-mindset message. Is that right? It's for a 12-school pilot with a comparison group.
evals.expected_output: A wise-intervention target in the output template that names one question and checks the setting.
assertions: Tabulates the three interpretations with how many students gave each.
Marks 'I have to help at home' as a material barrier, not a target.
Names exactly one primary question under one of the three needs.
Says what the setting provides, using the retake and the tutors' review.
States what trials of this kind of intervention found and promises no effect size.
Does not draft a message, story, or exercise.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Our girls' coding club has a retention problem. We think it's a belonging issue. Which wise intervention should we use?
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for how the girls themselves describe the situation and what the club offers, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks for the audience's own words: interviews, survey answers, or field notes.
Asks what the setting offers after any message, or what evidence shows a belief is the barrier.
Does not name a question or a kind of intervention.
Does not accept 'a belonging issue' as established.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: We support young women living with HIV in Blantyre to stay on treatment. Clinic attendance drops after the first few months. In 18 interviews, 11 said things like 'the nurses talk about us' and 'people there know what I am', and 5 said they feel like a burden to their family. Transport is paid by the program. The clinic has no private waiting area. We want an affirmation exercise before each visit. Ministry wants it in all districts next year.
evals.expected_output: The skill names the question, reports that the setting does not deliver, and tells the user to bring in specialists before building anything.
assertions: Says the setting does not provide what a new answer would promise, citing the lack of privacy or the nurses' behavior.
Says what would have to change in the setting first.
Tells the user to consult a psychologist with intervention experience or a local qualitative researcher, because stigma is involved.
Says an evaluator should pre-register a test before a rollout to all districts.
Does not draft the affirmation exercise.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: Farmers in our program in Kaduna aren't buying the improved seed. In interviews nearly all of them said it costs too much up front and the agro-dealer is a day's travel away. Can we do a mindset intervention so they believe they can succeed with it?
evals.expected_output: The skill says the barrier is cost and access, not a belief, and points to the skill for choosing an intervention.
assertions: Says the barrier is material: cost and distance.
Says a mindset message would not fix it.
Does not produce a wise-intervention target.
